properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 12 at 3:28PM PST until November 13 at 3:00PM PST by NWS Eureka CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Warning, Dangerously large breaking
waves 30 to 35 feet. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, High
astronomical tides will cause minor flooding in low lying areas
around Humboldt Bay. 1.5 to 2.2 feet of saltwater inundation
above ground level is possible near shorelines and tidal
waterways. Between 8.7 and 8.9 feet MLLW at the North Spit tide
gauge is predicted.

* WHERE...Northern Coastal Humboldt County.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Warning, from 1 PM Friday to 4 AM PST
Sunday. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 11 AM to 3 PM PST
Friday. High tide is at 1:04pm at the Humboldt Bay North Spit
tide gauge. Saltwater inundation will be possible 1 to 2 hours
before and after high tide.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of low lying areas around Humboldt Bay
including parks and roads with only isolated closures
expected. Flooding will likely impact Jackson Ranch Road in
the Arcata Bottoms and several roads in King Salmon. Breaking
waves can sweep people off jetties and docks, and into
dangerous seas. Life- threatening surf conditions and
significant beach erosion can be expected.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...While astronomical tides are decreasing
each day, persistent southerly winds are aiding in raising water
levels for Humboldt Bay. The beginning of a very large incoming
swell could enhance coastal flooding if they overlap, but they
aren't anticipated to do so or will not overlap for long. After
only brief improvement in high swell late Saturday through
Sunday, a second large swell is forecast late Sunday through
Monday.

properties.headline: High Surf Warning issued November 12 at 2:58PM PST until November 15 at 4:00AM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, An increased risk for
sneaker waves and strong rip currents with breaking waves of
15 to 20 ft expected. For the High Surf Warning, Dangerously
large breaking waves of 25 to 35 ft, with occasional sets of
40 to 50 ft at favored breakpoints. For the Coastal Flood
Advisory, large breaking waves will run up beaches and crash
over seawalls, inundating adjacent, low-lying infrastructure.

* WHERE...Coastal North Bay Including Point Reyes National
Seashore, San Francisco Peninsula Coast and Northern Monterey
Bay.

* WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, through Friday
afternoon. For the High Surf Warning, from 6 PM Friday to 4 AM
PST Sunday. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from midnight
Friday night to 6 PM PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. Dangerously large breaking waves can overpower
swimmers, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties,
and rocks resulting in significant physical injury and
increasing the risk of drowning. Waves can sweep across the
shoreline without warning, pulling people into the sea from
beaches, jetties, and rocks.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The Coastal Flood Advisory on Saturday is
specifically for the Pacific Coast, where large breaking waves
will spill over sea walls and run up beaches onto adjacent
infrastructure.

properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, dangerous rip currents
and breaking waves due to elevated surf. For the High Surf
Advisory, large breaking waves of 4 to 7 feet Friday, increasing
to 7 to 12 feet Saturday. Surf heights are expected to decrease
to 6 to 9 feet Sunday through Tuesday.

* WHERE...Malibu Coast and Los Angeles County Beaches. Surf will
we highest for west-northwest facing beaches.

afternoon. For the High Surf Advisory, from 2 PM Friday to 3
PM PST Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...There is an increased risk of ocean drowning. Rip
currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Waves can
wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats
nearshore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A series of significant west-northwesterly

potentially again Monday. There is potential for moderate

these impacts may be moderate to significant beach erosion and
shallow flooding of normal dry beaches and walkways.

properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued November 11 at 11:29AM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...The South Coast AQMD has extended an air quality alert due
to harmful levels of fine particle pollution.
Visit https://www.aqmd.gov/alertinfo to check current and forecasted
air quality levels.

* WHERE...in Vernon, Maywood, Bell Gardens, Westmont, Hawthorne,
Inglewood, Downtown LA, East LA and Huntington Park. Levels of
particle pollution can vary by time and location depending on
emissions and local weather conditions.

* WHEN...until 11:59 PM Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Particle pollution can get deep into the lungs and cause
serious health problems such as heart attacks, bronchitis, asthma
attacks, and difficulty breathing. Everyone can be affected, but
sensitive groups such as people with lung or heart disease, older
adults, people who are pregnant, children, and those who spend a lot
of time outdoors are at greater risk.
properties.instruction:
To protect your health, check air quality levels and act as needed:

* When Air Quality Index (AQI) levels are "Unhealthy for
Sensitive Groups" (orange), sensitive groups as specified
above should limit extended or intense outdoor activity.
* When AQI is "Unhealthy" (red), everyone may experience health
impacts. Sensitive groups should avoid extended time outdoors.
* When AQI is "Very Unhealthy" (purple), sensitive groups should
avoid all outdoor physical activity. Everyone else should
avoid extended or intense outdoor activity.
* When AQI is "Hazardous" (maroon), everyone should avoid all
outdoor physical activity.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

To help keep indoor air clean when air quality is poor:

* Keep windows and doors closed
* Run your air conditioner and/or an air purifier
* Do not use whole house fans or swamp coolers that bring in
outside air if you have other methods to stay cool
* Avoid other sources of pollution such as fireplaces, candles,
incense, grilling, and gasoline-powered lawn and garden
equipment
